# `crates/tf_tree_ingest/testdata` — provenance

## `zstd_conformance.mcap` (1 069 bytes)

**Not a recording.** Nothing here came off a robot. It is the evidence that the
pure-Rust zstd decoder in `crate::decompress` agrees with **libzstd**, not merely
with the `ruzstd` encoder that writes every other compressed fixture. An encoder
and decoder from one crate can agree and both disagree with the zstd `rosbag2` and
Foxglove link; the other fixtures prove round-trip, this one proves conformance.

### What is ours and what is libzstd's

| Part | Produced by |
| --- | --- |
| MCAP magic, `Header`, `Chunk`/`DataEnd`/`Footer` framing | `tf_tree_ingest::fixture::chunked_mcap_bytes` |
| `Schema`, `Channel`, `Message` bodies; the CDR payloads | `tf_tree_ingest::fixture` + `tf_tree_ingest::cdr::encode_tf_message` |
| Each chunk's `uncompressed_size` and `uncompressed_crc` (CRC32 over the *uncompressed* records) | this repository, before compression |
| **Each chunk's `records` field — the compressed bytes** | **libzstd, via the `zstd` CLI** |

Our CRC32 over our own input is what checks libzstd's output.

### Generation

```text
$ cargo run -p tf_tree_ingest --features fixture --example gen_zstd_conformance
wrote …/crates/tf_tree_ingest/testdata/zstd_conformance.mcap (1069 B, 3 chunks, from 1982 uncompressed B) using *** Zstandard CLI (64-bit) v1.5.5, by Yann Collet ***
```

Regeneration is byte-reproducible on zstd 1.5.5 (`cmp` clean), so a diff means the
corpus or the compressor changed. Each chunk's records go through
`zstd -19 --no-check -c -q`: `-19` exercises longer matches and larger Huffman
tables; `--no-check` omits zstd's content checksum **on purpose**, because nothing
in `crate::decompress` verifies it and the chunk CRC32 is the check that runs.

Regenerate only when `fixture::conformance_recording` changes:
`tests/ingest.rs`'s `a_real_libzstd_recording_ingests` compares the committed file
against a control written from that function.

### Licence

Every byte is generated by code in this repository (MIT OR Apache-2.0) plus
`zstd`'s output, which carries no licence of its own. No third-party content is
vendored.

### lz4

There is no lz4 *file* here (no `lz4` CLI on the host). The gap is closed by
`decompress::tests::a_hand_authored_lz4_frame_decodes_per_the_specification`: an
82-byte frame written by hand from the frame and block formats, which `lz4_flex`'s
encoder does **not** produce, and of whose 656 single-bit perturbations 651 are
caught (the five that are not are enumerated in the test). It lives in source, with
no regenerating recipe, because a regenerated vector is a round-trip again. A whole
independently-written lz4 `.mcap` (from the `lz4` or `mcap` CLI) would land beside
this file with its own row.
